summary: Firestore and Storage use default-deny rules, strict ownership and validation. Administrative authorization now relies on a backend-managed custom claim. Account deletion is implemented as an App Check-protected callable function because privileged cleanup cannot safely run in the client.

findings.result: Rules require request.auth.token.admin == true. No email address grants backend access.
The callable deletes data only for request.auth.uid and requires App Check plus authentication no older than five minutes. It must be deployed before release.
traps and schools are intentionally public. Personal data, internal notes and moderation metadata must not be stored in those documents.
Rules validate writes but do not provide business-level request quotas. Add backend throttling and monitoring before material production traffic.

releaseRequirements: Deploy functions, Firestore rules, indexes and Storage rules to the intended Firebase project.
Set admin custom claims only from a trusted Admin SDK environment.
Restrict public client keys and protect service accounts with least-privilege IAM.
Monitor valid App Check traffic before enabling enforcement for Firebase products.
Configure and verify RevenueCat webhook authorization and idempotency.
